title: The Afternoon Brief: Injuries reshape NFL rosters; Lakers sale hits record $12.5B
dek: The NFL preseason brought a wave of injury updates and strategic roster decisions as teams navigate health concerns heading into the regular season. Across sports, major business news emerged in basketball and soccer governance.
author: GoCheckMySports
key_fact: Ricky Pearsall's PCL surgery and nine-month recovery timeline takes the 49ers receiver out for all of 2026, forcing the team to reshape its receiving corps while Carson Beck's rib injury and Josh Allen's full participation in Buffalo's Highmark Stadium debut define the preseason injury landscape.
bottom_line: The NFL preseason weekend brought injury updates that reshape rosters for 2026, with Pearsall out for the season targeting 2027, Beck sidelined briefly as a precaution, and Allen cleared to play. A record Lakers sale and Westbrook's retirement marked major business milestones in basketball, while Infantino faces organized opposition from major confederations in FIFA governance, and Bertman's death closes a major chapter in college baseball history. Watch for Pearsall's recovery timeline, Allen's actual playing time Saturday, the Lakers sale's September board approval, and the November 18 FIFA challenger deadline.
body: The NFL preseason weekend crystallized a series of roster-altering injury decisions and ownership changes that will reverberate through the season. On the injury front, San Francisco's Ricky Pearsall underwent PCL repair surgery targeting a nine-month recovery and a 2027 return after the team's initial decision to rehabilitate the knee conservatively failed when swelling developed during training camp. Pearsall's injury, originally sustained in a Week 4 loss to Jacksonville last season, marks a second significant obstacle in his three-year career marked by limited availability. Meanwhile, Arizona's Carson Beck sat out Thursday's preseason game against Las Vegas as a precaution following a rib injury sustained during the Hall of Fame Game, though team sources described the injury as not serious with zero long-term concern. In contrast, Buffalo's Josh Allen is active and set to play Saturday at the new Highmark Stadium against Carolina, a full starter approach that represents a shift from the prior coaching regime's preseason caution.

Off the field, the Los Angeles Lakers ownership landscape moved sharply when Mark Walter agreed to sell the franchise to a group led by Josh Kushner and Bob Iger for $12.5 billion, a record price for a professional sports franchise. The figure marks roughly a quarter rise from the $10 billion valuation at which Walter took controlling interest in October 2025. The sale remains agreed, not closed, and requires approval from the NBA board of governors, which next meets in September.

Across other sports, Russell Westbrook announced his retirement after 18 NBA seasons as the league's all-time triple-double leader with 209, along with 27,176 career points and 10,351 assists. Katie Ledecky extended her 1,500 freestyle winning streak to 16 years at the Pan Pacific Championships in Irvine, holding off Australia's Lani Pallister in 15:36.09, her closest finish in the event in 13 years. A U.S. quartet of Will Modglin, Van Mathias, Gretchen Walsh and Kate Douglass lowered the mixed medley relay world record to 3:36.70. In soccer, FIFA President Gianni Infantino secured backing from six Arab federations on Thursday as UEFA, CONCACAF, and AFC jointly condemned his withdrawn $20 billion World Cup privatization proposal. The three continental confederations and several national associations have withdrawn support for his 2027 reelection, with UEFA warning of a boycott of FIFA games. Celta Vigo's La Liga season opener against Osasuna was postponed from August 17 to August 27 due to a fungal outbreak at Estadio de Balaidos, though Osasuna disputed the rescheduling, citing a prior agreement to play during the international break instead.

In college sports, legendary LSU baseball coach Skip Bertman died Friday morning at 88. Bertman built LSU into a college baseball dynasty with five Men's College World Series titles, 870 career wins, and 11 MCWS appearances. He later served as LSU's athletic director, overseeing football national championships in 2003 and 2007.
